body:
Instead of checking every shortcut, we should instead track text changes and caret position changes to automatically cancel it instead.
This looks like it doesn't account for using the menu to undo or cut. Also redo. Also probably shift + word left/right.

> Instead of checking every shortcut, we should instead track text changes and caret position changes to automatically cancel it instead. This looks like it doesn't account for using the menu to undo or cut. Also redo. Also probably shift + word left/right.

Thanks for the feedback! Actually I have realized there are even more shortcuts than that, like `CTRL` + `Shift` + `Left`/`Right`, `Shift` + `Home`, or `Shift` + `End`, which this solution didn't account for after testing it again today. I guess these can just be good test cases, in addition to the shortcuts I have already mentioned, to ensure the desync issues are fixed though.

I've updated the code to check if the caret position has changed, which should fix this issue regarding shortcut desyncing autocompletion as I've tested. I'm not sure it's necessary to track specific text changes however since issues seem to only arise when the caret moves. Just as a note, I still canceled code completion manually for these shortcuts because they do an early return:

- `CTRL` + `Shift` + `K`
- `CTRL` + `Shift` + `J`
- `CTRL` + `Enter`
- `CTRL` + `Shift` + `Enter`

It is more complex than checking if the caret moved at all, as long as the caret is still on the text being completed it can move left and right and it shouldn't cancel in those cases. Same when typing or removing text on it.
So we probably need to use `code_completion_base` or something to determine when the caret column is out of bounds.

We can use the `"caret_changed"` signal to know when it changes even outside of `gui_input` so it works from the edit menu too. And then we don't have to manually cancel for some shortcuts either.

> It is more complex than checking if the caret moved at all, as long as the caret is still on the text being completed it can move left and right and it shouldn't cancel in those cases. Same when typing or removing text on it.

@kitbdev Moving left/right as well as typing/removing text is already accounted for in this solution, so this shouldn't be a problem.

> So we probably need to use code_completion_base or something to determine when the caret column is out of bounds.
> We can use the "caret_changed" signal to know when it changes even outside of gui_input so it works from the edit menu too. And then we don't have to manually cancel for some shortcuts either.

Hmm, this opens up more opportunities for code completion to work improperly since like you have said, going left, right, deleting, or typing text would also move the caret. In those cases, you would want to filter the code completion options when needed with `_filter_code_completion_candidates_impl()` as the code written in `gui_input` already does before any of my changes.

It might be worth giving it a try to avoid manually canceling code completion for some shortcuts, but it will take some reworking as lots of code already here seems to deal with that logic.

Just like how pressing `Home` or `End` has canceled code completion manually before, the logic I have written here will do similarly with the shortcuts I have mentioned. (Actually, I think technically the `Home` and `End` actions don't need to cancel code completion manually anymore since I check caret changes here)

This still relies on users manually cancelling the code completion when needed, The menu like I mentioned: I found a few more places it needs to be cancelled too: - adding a function in `ScriptTextEditor::add_callback` - Create code region shortcut (if you started with a selection) - Fold all lines shortcut - Comment line shortcut - Evaluate selection shortcut (If selecting text like `PI`) And some places where text changes need to be considered: - `TextEditorBase::reload_text` - pasting into a selection of the same length (or maybe it can just refilter idk) - and undo/redo of this There might be some more hidden ones, anything that changes the caret position or text could need it. This approach helps for many shortcuts, but we still need to manually cancel it for some other shortcuts and everywhere else needed and we still need to keep it in mind whenever new things are added. The solution I'm imagining would work for all cases and CodeEdit users wouldn't be expected to have to cancel it if they move the caret through code. And we could also remove many existing `cancel_code_completion()` calls. It will be more tricky to get the logic right for things like moving the caret left and right, but I don't think it will be too bad.

Think I will convert this to draft, I can confirm the edge cases which you have mentioned also desync autocompletion after some testing out, which isn't good.

Also probably not a good idea to rely on too much manual cancelling since there could be more methods/shortcuts added that could cause a similar issue again if this isn't accounted for, so that's a good point. Guess technically the solution worked great for majority of shortcuts, but I could still miss some even after that.

I'll work on trying to find a solution that'll cancel code completion while tracking caret changes which you mentioned earlier, and text changes. Of course, accounting for changes that are normal, like left/right, deleting, or typing which would normally filter the autocomplete. Also changes like `Alt` + `up`/`down` that are caret changes but should keep autocomplete open without changes.

I'll also look into the method you mentioned earlier relating to the `"caret_changed"` signal to see how it'll go, and see if I can come up with a solution regarding all the edge cases we've mentioned so far without needing to do any manual canceling. Also probably look at other `cancel_code_completion` calls, to see if they're necessary after such changes like you mentioned as well. 

(Don't think I will touch the `End` action I have mentioned earlier, that cancels code completion, in case people are already used to hitting something like `End` to end autocomplete I guess.)

Sounds good! And for the text changes the `lines_edited_from` signal may be helpful. > Also changes like Alt + up/down that are caret changes but should keep autocomplete open without changes. For moving the line up/down it wouldn't be unexpected that it cancels. Actually it can lead to invalid cases, like when moving a line into a multiline string or comment:

> For moving the line up/down it wouldn't be unexpected that it cancels. Actually it can lead to invalid cases, like when moving a line into a multiline string or comment: That's a good point, I guess it doesn't "desync" like the rest of the shortcuts/actions do here where you could accept the code completion option without it breaking, but it technically still breaks in that way. Also you could run some local variables out of scope like this lol: `CTRL` + `/` and `CTRL` + `K` (toggle comment) is alike in that it wouldn't error out if you accepted the code completion, but obviously code completion doesn't activate in comments so it's not normal. So I think it's obviously best to close their code completion since they can be misleading. In any case, I have reworked the PR so that I use the `"caret_changed"` and `"text_changed"` signals to see if any caret columns/lines are different from the last time the code completion was filtered. Normal actions that filter code completion like typing, moving `left` or `right`, and `Backspace` wouldn't be canceled, but anything else will cancel it. Also accounted for the really rare case when text changes, but caret pos doesn't, like replacing/pasting a selected word/line with something of the same length which would've also desynced code autocompletion. These signals seem to be emitted with call_deferred, so I think I can assume they will be called after `_filter_code_completion_candidates_impl()`, which needs to run before any of the checks I do in `text_changed` and the new `line_col_changed` method I added. Additionally, I removed some `cancel_code_completion()` calls which included coverage for these actions previously, since this more generalized solution will fix them up too after testing: - `Ctrl` + `.`/`,` (Go to next/previous breakpoint) - `Ctrl` + `G` (Go to line) - `Ctrl` + `B` (Go to next bookmark) - `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `B` (Go to previous bookmark) - `Home`
